title: Finally understanding Parker's chord extensions
summary: After weeks of not grasping why Parker's notes lay outside his chords, it clicks that he plays extensions, changing Malachi's whole musical outlook.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: So many incidents... Oh, that band was just a learning thing about life and about music and everything else... For the first two or three days in the band, or I should say for

the first couple of weeks in the band, I did not realize what Charlie Parker was doing. I heard him playing, and I could hear these things he was playing, but it wasn't like anything I had heard before. And the chords I was playing on the piano wasn't... A lot of things he would play that was not in the chords! Which I learned later that he was playing extensions of the chord. If I was playing a seventh or a ninth, he was probably playing something above that, an eleventh or augmented eleventh or thirteenth, something that paralleled what I was playing, but not... I had been used to guys playing the notes in the chord that I played, you know. And it was a thing that I had to get used to.

One night I was playing on the bandstand, and I happened to... Something rang in my ears, and it was just like a lightbulb came on, and all of a sudden it dawned on me what he was doing. I think it was one of the greatest enlightenments that I've ever had.. Because it was a turning point in my whole musical outlook, on everything. And I can truthfully say that everything that I'm doing now, my whole musical concept was enhanced, I think, more by Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie than anyone else I know. I shouldn't say anyone else I know. I should say other than pianists that I knew. I can't give enough credit to Dizzy Gillespie, because to me he is one of the greatest musicians I have ever...
